solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the blog titled it No 28289, which the sequence puts at 29289

entries.clue: Casino is accountable to some degree over incident (8)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside it
in a clue read across, 'over' turns the letters back to front

annotation.surface: A gambling house is being held partly responsible for something that happened on its floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits inside the first three words, but backwards; reading it right to left gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular happening or event, so it matches incident.

entries.clue: Tea second, milk mostly first for English tea maker (9)

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its last letter goes
take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

annotation.surface: Instructions for brewing: tea, then milk, in a particular order, as an Englishman makes his cuppa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea maker' looks like a person or a kettle, but it is the plant whose flowers make a herbal tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Chamomile is the plant whose dried flowers are steeped to make chamomile tea, so it makes tea.

entries.clue: Lab mice breaking scientific equipment (7)

indicators.note: breaking the words apart lets their letters be rearranged

annotation.surface: Escaped laboratory mice are wrecking the apparatus.
annotation.walkthrough: The lab setting makes 'scientific equipment' feel like part of the story rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus used by alchemists and early chemists.

entries.clue: Home originally included guest facilities (5)

indicators.note: take the original, that is first, letters

blocks.note: first letters of Included and Guest
'the facilities' is a polite word for the toilet; a loo is a toilet

annotation.surface: A house that from the start came with a guest bathroom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' in the sense of a lavatory is the step to see; loo is the everyday British word for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit dwelling, a home.

entries.clue: Sleep regularly enfolds (3)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: eNfOlDs: second, fourth and sixth letters

annotation.surface: Sleep wraps around you, night after night.
annotation.walkthrough: The land of Nod is sleep, and to nod off is to fall asleep, so NOD stands for sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: Nod means sleep, as in the land of Nod or a quick nod in an armchair.

entries.clue: Reflect in silence, taking in one small wrong (6)

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder quietly
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Quiet reflection helps someone come to terms with a minor injustice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' here is the verb, to treat someone badly, which is what misuse means.
annotation.definitionFit: To misuse someone is to treat them badly, to wrong them.

entries.clue: Former kingdom’s obsession involving Conservative European party (9)

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the pieces that follow

annotation.surface: A historic realm's fixation with a right-wing continental political party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' sits beside Conservative and European and reads as a political party, but it is the social kind: a do.
annotation.definitionFit: Macedonia was the ancient kingdom of Philip II and Alexander the Great.

entries.clue: Bird down (7)

blocks.note: to down a drink, a verb here

annotation.walkthrough: 'Down' tempts you toward feathers, which fits a bird, but it is the verb: to down a pint.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: a common fork-tailed bird, and the verb for gulping a drink, which 'down' is a plain synonym of.

entries.clue: Group of geese hide around rear of farmhouse (5)

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second
take the last letter of the word

blocks.note: a hide is an animal skin

annotation.surface: Geese on the farm hide round the back of the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb for the geese, but it is the noun, an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A skein is the collective noun for geese in flight.

entries.clue: Mischievous girl missing home match (4)

indicators.note: the named piece is taken out

blocks.note: a gamine is an impish, boyish girl
at home = in; this is removed from GAMINE

annotation.surface: A naughty girl skips the home fixture.
annotation.walkthrough: The sporting surface makes 'home match' read as one phrase, but 'home' belongs to the wordplay and 'match' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single contest in a sport, such as a football fixture, is called either.

entries.clue: Couple perhaps finally renovate large part of church (4,6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word

blocks.note: a lady and a chap make a couple; 'perhaps' flags an example

annotation.surface: A couple are at last restoring much of the church building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple' is not a number but a pair of people, one lady and one chap.
annotation.definitionFit: A lady chapel is a chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary within a larger church.

entries.clue: Behold to-do when running wild (3-7)

indicators.note: letters that run about are free to change places

annotation.surface: Look at the commotion when something gets out of control.
annotation.walkthrough: A to-do is a fuss; here it just supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Hot-blooded means passionate and easily roused, so wild in temper.

entries.clue: Furniture one found in theatre (7)

blocks.note: a sideboard with open shelves above for plates
the backstage helper who gets actors into costume

annotation.surface: A piece of furniture turns up among the props of a playhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a prop on stage; the second meaning is a person backstage.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a kitchen cabinet for crockery, and the theatre worker who dresses the cast.

entries.clue: Hunter relates to the audience (4)

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so a word that sounds like another

blocks.note: relates = links, as in links one thing to another

annotation.surface: A hunter tells his tale to listeners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hunter' suggests a person, but it is a predator: the wild cat.
annotation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat that hunts hares and deer.

entries.clue: Separated daughter is coming to Greek island (8)

blocks.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

annotation.surface: A daughter living apart from her family travels to a Greek island.
annotation.walkthrough: Discrete (separate) is not discreet (tactful); the letters from Crete settle the spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct.

entries.clue: Underground traveller initially travels hours absorbed in catchy music (9)

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the first letter of travels is used
the pieces go inside the next word

blocks.note: an earworm is a tune you cannot get out of your head

annotation.surface: A Tube commuter loses whole hours lost in a tune stuck in his head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underground traveller' paints a London Tube passenger, but the traveller really moves through soil.
annotation.definitionFit: An earthworm burrows through the ground, travelling underground.

entries.clue: A single desire, but not old, somewhat recent (6)

indicators.note: take the first piece without the second

blocks.note: one wish is a single desire

annotation.surface: Someone who wants only one thing, nothing old, just something fairly new.
annotation.walkthrough: The old/recent contrast in the surface makes 'not old' look like part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Newish means fairly new, somewhat recent.

entries.clue: Put over with great attitude (9)

blocks.note: a pose is an attitude, a way of holding the body

annotation.surface: Someone gets their point across with real panache.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put over' in the sense of communicating is the natural reading, but here it means to lay one thing on top of another.
annotation.definitionFit: To superpose is to place one thing over another.

entries.clue: Tricky question when the time of Christian festival has moved (6)

indicators.note: a letter has shifted position within the word

blocks.note: the letter T of the festival, the only letter that moves
the spring festival; its T goes to the front

annotation.surface: A puzzle about why the date of Easter shifts from year to year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The time' is the letter T of EASTER, and only that one letter moves, to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a teaser is short for brain-teaser, a puzzling question.

entries.clue: Evolving entails forward projection (7)

indicators.note: letters that evolve change their order

annotation.surface: Development involves looking ahead and forecasting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Projection' reads as a forecast; in fact it is something jutting out, like a bulge in a battle line.
annotation.definitionFit: A salient is a part of a front line or fortification that projects forward.

entries.clue: Second phaeton ordered for another carriage (8)

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: A second horse-drawn phaeton is booked in place of a different carriage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' is fair because a phaeton is itself a carriage; the answer is a light open one-seated carriage.
annotation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light, open, horse-drawn carriage, named after its designer.

entries.clue: Hertfordshire town’s success in protecting church (7)

indicators.note: the outer pieces wrap around and guard the inner one

annotation.surface: A small town's triumph in saving its local church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a joining word but is wordplay too: 'success in' forms the pair of outer pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the answer is a real market town north of London, in the English county of Hertfordshire.

entries.clue: Blue-eyed boy in swimming pool, length behind (4)

indicators.note: the named letter goes to the back

blocks.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool; its L is the letter that moves
L = length, shifted from the front of LIDO to the back

annotation.surface: The favourite lad is in the pool, a length behind the others.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue-eyed boy' is a British phrase for a favourite, someone who can do no wrong.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'blue-eyed boy' is British slang for someone adored and favoured, which is what an idol is.

entries.clue: Drink before a show? (5)

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky
used as it stands; 'before' puts DRAM first

annotation.surface: A pre-theatre tipple.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark points to the joke: a drink before a show is exactly what the letters spell, DRAM before A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stage or screen play is one kind of show.

entries.clue: Bequeathed present journal containing tons (10)

indicators.note: the word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: present = here, as in a register

annotation.surface: A diary full of tons of entries is handed down as a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as a gift, which fits bequeathed, but it means here.
annotation.definitionFit: Hereditary means passed down from one generation to the next, as a bequest is.

entries.clue: Hold back when accepting odd bits of true fact (5)

indicators.note: the first word takes the next piece inside it
take the first, third and so on letters

blocks.note: to dam water is to hold it back

annotation.surface: Someone holds off on admitting even the odd scrap of truth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold back' looks like restraint, but it is a dam holding back water.
annotation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a fact.

entries.clue: Man keeping deep affection back, heartless not spiteful (10)

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece inside it
the word is written backwards
remove the middle, leaving the outside letters

annotation.surface: A man hides his deep love, and his coldness is not meant unkindly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ends on 'not spiteful', but 'not' is wordplay and 'spiteful' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, spiteful.

entries.clue: Finish repair to remove marks (3)

indicators.note: the named letter is taken out

blocks.note: M = marks, the old German currency; removed from MEND

annotation.surface: A final repair job to get rid of stains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marks' sounds like smudges to be cleaned off, but it is the abbreviation M for the German mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to bring something to a close, as in finishing or ending a job.

entries.clue: Possibly tire of work on house (4)

blocks.note: op = opus, a work; 'on' puts it after HO

annotation.surface: Maybe someone is sick of working on the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tire' reads as the verb, to grow weary, but it is the old spelling of tyre: the iron band on a wheel, a kind of hoop.
annotation.definitionFit: A tire, the metal rim round a cartwheel, is one kind of hoop.

entries.clue: One fighting to censor The Scotsman’s coverage (6)

blocks.note: a tam, or tam-o'-shanter, is a Scottish woollen cap

annotation.surface: A campaigner battles to suppress a newspaper's reporting.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is a real Edinburgh newspaper, so 'coverage' reads as news reporting; it is headgear, the tam.
annotation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small fighting cock, and a bantamweight is a boxer.

entries.clue: One getting something done about pit boss (8)

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the next

blocks.note: a doer is one who gets things done
a pit is a coal mine

annotation.surface: A man who gets things done, running the whole coal mine as its boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the verb here, to boss people about.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in verb form: both mean to lord it over people and order them about.
